a

b

c

d
t=0,v=0
e

Submit

decision.explanation: Velocity is v(t)=s'(t)=3t^2-12t, and acceleration is a(t)=v'(t)=6t-12. Setting acceleration equal to zero gives t=2. Then v(2)=12-24=-12.

after.name: Question 1
after.problem:
A particle $P$ is traveling along the $x$-axis with displacement $s(t)$ from a fixed origin $O$ given by

$$
s(t)={t}^{3}-6{t}^{2},\,t\ge 0.
$$

Find the time at which the acceleration is zero, and find the value of the velocity at this moment.
after.worked_solution:
First, we calculate $v(t)$ by differentiating $s(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\frac{\text{d}s}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{3}-6{t}^{2}) \\  & =3{t}^{2}-12t\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now, we differentiate $v(t)$ to find $a(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}a(t) & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3{t}^{2}-12t) \\  & =6t-12\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we put $a=0$ to find the time when the acceleration is zero:

$$
\begin{aligned}0 & =6t-12 \\ 6t & =12 \\ t & =2\end{aligned}
$$

So the acceleration is zero when $t=2.$ To find the velocity at this moment, we substitute this back into $v(t)$ to get

$$
v(2)=3(2)^{2}-12(2)=-12.
$$

decision.explanation: By the product rule, v(t)=s'(t)=4e^t+(4t-7)e^t=(4t-3)e^t. Since e^t>0, the particle moves in the direction of increasing x when 4t-3>0, so t is in (3/4, infinity).

after.name: Question 2
after.problem:
The displacement $s,$ in meters, relative to a fixed origin $O$ of a particle moving in a straight line along the $x$-axis is given by $s(t)=(4t-7){e}^{t},$ where $t>0$ is the time, measured in seconds. Find the time intervals in which the particle is moving in the direction of increasing $x.$

$t\in (${{field-1}},

{{field-2}}$)$
after.worked_solution:
If the particle moves in the direction of increasing $x,$ then its velocity is positive. 

First, we calculate the velocity function by differentiating the position function:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\frac{\text{d}s}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}((4t-7){e}^{t}) \\  & =4{e}^{t}+(4t-7){e}^{t} \\  & =(4t-3){e}^{t}\end{aligned}
$$

To calculate time intervals in which the particle is moving in the direction of increasing $x$, we solve $v(t)>0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & >0 \\ (4t-3){e}^{t} & >0 \\ 4t-3 & >0 \\ t & >\frac{3}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the time interval in which the particle is moving to the direction of increasing $x$ is 

$$
t\in (\frac{3}{4},\infty ).
$$
